title: The Art of Staying Ahead of Deadlines Improved Algorithms for the Minimum Tardy Processing Time

predicted_errors.error_location: Section “Leveraging Dynamic Strings,” construction of the shift and trimming strings
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated split convention is inclusive: split(x,i) creates x[0..i] and x(i..|x|]. Therefore splitting 0^u at position p_j produces a left string of p_j+1 zeros, not 0^{p_j} as claimed. Likewise, splitting a string at u retains positions 0 through u, i.e. u+1 positions under the paper's own interval notation, rather than trimming it to length u. The proposed operations consequently shift L_{j-1} by p_j+1 rather than p_j and retain the wrong length, so they do not implement the stated dynamic-program transition.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section “Leveraging Dynamic Strings,” initialization: “build 0^u by inserting the word w=0 and self-concatenating it log u times”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Repeated self-concatenation doubles the length each time. Starting from one zero and performing log u doublings yields a string of length 2^{log u}, which equals u only when u is an exact power of two (and depends on an unstated rounding convention otherwise). Since u=d_max+1 is arbitrary, this procedure generally does not construct 0^u. A binary-length construction and appropriate truncation would be required.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section “Leveraging Dynamic Strings,” use of split(0^u,p_j)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The algorithm assumes that every p_j can be used as a split position in a string of size u=d_max+1. Standard instances need not satisfy p_j<=d_max: a job with p_j>d_j is simply necessarily tardy and may occur in the input. For example, one job with p_j=10 and d_j=5 gives u=6, but the prescribed split at p_j=10 is outside the string and is invalid. Such jobs can be discarded in O(n) preprocessing, but the paper neither states nor performs that necessary step.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section “Leveraging Dynamic Strings,” initialization of the dynamic-program state
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The construction initializes a zero string but never constructs or inserts the indicator string for the required base state S_0={0}, which must have a 1 in position 0. A zero string represents the empty reachable-sum set, not {0}; starting the recurrence from it would keep all S_j empty. The missing base-state construction is essential for correctness.

The text repeatedly relies on citations [1] through [8], including the central Fischer--Wennmann algorithm [5], the dynamic-string data structure [6,7], and the claimed prior running times [2,4,8]. However, the supplied bibliography contains only entries [9], [10], and [11]. Thus the main attributions cannot be checked and the cited sources for the paper's core algorithmic claims are absent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction to Lawler and Moore’s algorithm and subsequent references to “Eq. (3b)” and “Eq. (3c)”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper says that S_0,...,S_n are defined “as in the following,” but no recurrence or Equation (3) is present in the supplied text. Later sections rely on the undefined Eq. (3b) and Eq. (3c) to justify the split, shift, and trimming operations.
